title: Microsegmented Competitor Behavior Matrix & Prospect Impact Metrics
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Goal: Produce an actionable, microsegmented matrix that maps competitor provider behavior (availability, price shocks, latency windows, quantization/compatibility changes) to prospect impact scores for enterprise buyer cohorts. This artifact will be used by sales engineering and product marketing to prioritize model onboarding, fallback policies, and procurement triggers.

Scope:
- Universe: tracked public/open model providers + top 6 closed-source LLM vendors we monitor.
- Segments: SMB SaaS, Mid-market product teams, Regulated enterprise (FinServ/Health), Platform teams.
- Time window: rolling 90-day behavior signals + 12-month supply-change indicator.
- Outputs: 1) CSV matrix for programmatic scoring, 2) 2-page executive brief, 3) one interactive Grafana/Looker dashboard.

Why this is different: previous landscape docs focused on single-dimension scoring (latency or cost). This work stitches short-term behavior (release cadence, outages, quantization changes) with prospect-level sensitivity metrics to produce dynamic prospect impact ranks. That enables targeted outreach and prioritization of fallback model commitments for Redwood Dedicated/Private offers.
success_metrics: Top-40 enterprise prospects assigned a prospect-impact score within 2 weeks
Reduce estimated fallback provisioning cost for top 10 accounts by 18% within next quarter
Dashboard updated daily with automated signal ingestion; <24h alerting on supply shock for critical model families

risks: Signal quality: vendor release tags are inconsistent; false positives may inflate outage counts
Overfitting weights: prospect rubric calibrated to a narrow sales sample — may bias priority toward existing relationships
Operational cost: frequent dashboard updates and alerts may generate noise without throttling / priority filters
